overall_status: PHYSICAL VALIDATION BLOCKED — EXTERNAL AWS AUTHORIZATION REQUIRED

blockers.description: Terraform binary missing / not configured in system PATH
blockers.root_cause: Host workstation did not have Terraform installed in default system environment
blockers.proposed_fix: Install HashiCorp Terraform v1.16.4 via WinGet package manager and verify executable path

blockers.description: Terraform infrastructure module formatting and syntax validation
blockers.root_cause: Terraform files in infra/terraform needed canonical formatting, module download, and provider schema validation
blockers.proposed_fix: Execute terraform fmt, terraform init, and terraform validate on infra/terraform
blockers.evidence: terraform fmt -check returned 0; terraform init downloaded AWS & Kubernetes modules; terraform validate returned "Success! The configuration is valid."

blockers.description: AWS credentials unavailable on host environment
blockers.root_cause: No AWS access keys, session tokens, or SSO profiles configured in ~/.aws or environment variables
blockers.required_external_action: User / Account Administrator must configure AWS credentials via `aws configure` or set environment variables AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, and AWS_SESSION_TOKEN
blockers.proposed_fix: Authenticate to target AWS account with sufficient IAM permissions (EKS, EC2, RDS, ElastiCache, VPC, ALB)
blockers.evidence: terraform plan probe failed with: "Error: No valid credential sources found" and ~/.aws directory is empty

blockers.description: High-scale vCPU quotas and cloud budget allocation required for 1M VU physical topology
blockers.root_cause: 640 vCPUs (20x c6i.4xlarge + 40x c6i.2xlarge) exceed standard default AWS account vCPU limits (standard limit is 32-64 vCPUs)
blockers.required_external_action: Submit AWS Service Quotas increase for "Running On-Demand Standard (A, C, D, H, I, M, R, T, Z) instances" to >= 640 vCPUs and authorize test execution budget (~$650)
blockers.proposed_fix: Approve Service Quota increase and allocate cloud execution budget
blockers.evidence: Audited in qa/physical/aws/SERVICE_QUOTA_AUDIT.md requiring 640 EC2 vCPUs, 128 Aurora vCPUs, and 96 ElastiCache vCPUs

blockers.description: Distributed 40-node EC2 Linux load generator fleet unprovisioned
blockers.root_cause: Requires AWS credential authorization and quota approval to provision via Terraform
blockers.required_external_action: Provision via `terraform apply` after resolving BLK-003 and BLK-004
blockers.proposed_fix: Deploy 40x c6i.2xlarge load generator worker instances in private subnets with k6 distributed runner
blockers.evidence: Local host is a single Windows machine bounded at 22,400 Winsock sockets; 0 EC2 generator instances active

blockers.description: Physical EKS cluster, ALB ingress, Aurora PostgreSQL cluster, and ElastiCache Redis cluster unprovisioned
blockers.root_cause: Requires AWS cloud infrastructure deployment via Terraform
blockers.required_external_action: Provision cloud resources via `terraform apply` after resolving BLK-003 and BLK-004
blockers.proposed_fix: Deploy full infrastructure blueprint from infra/terraform/
blockers.evidence: 0 active cloud nodes; kubectl connection refused against local stub

blockers.description: Local Windows workstation socket buffer ceiling (WSAENOBUFS 10055)
blockers.root_cause: Windows OS ephemeral Winsock memory pool limit restricts single-host concurrent socket count to 22,400
blockers.required_external_action: None for local scale; resolved at high scale by distributing load across 40 Linux EC2 generator nodes
blockers.proposed_fix: Maintain validated single-host threshold at 10,000 VUs / 1,373.3 RPS; distribute 1M VU load across 40 Linux EC2 instances (25K VUs/node)
blockers.evidence: Host benchmark verified 10,000 VUs passing SLA; >22,400 VUs triggers OS socket buffer exhaustion
